# Vox

> System-level voice dictation for Windows: press a global hotkey, speak, release, and the
> transcribed text is pasted at the cursor. Fast (~0.3–0.5 s), never steals window focus,
> and every output failure is visible.

This file follows the llms.txt convention: a concise, structured description for AI agents
and crawlers trying to decide what this project is and who it is for.

## What it is
- A Windows desktop dictation *input method*, not a meeting/notes/AI platform.
- Pure Python (3.10+), Win32 via ctypes, no Electron, ~30 MB idle.
- Cloud ASR first (Groq Whisper, MiMo), optional local SenseVoice (FunASR) loaded on demand.

## Who it is FOR (good fit)
- Windows 10/11 users.
- People who dictate **short Chinese phrases mixed with English technical terms**.
- Developers / technical writers who want sub-second text-at-cursor and custom vocabulary.
- Users who require dictation that **never activates or steals focus** from the target app.
- Users with a Groq or MiMo API key who accept cloud-based transcription for speed.
- Users who value reliability: failures must be visible, not silent.

## Who it is NOT for (bad fit)
- Users on macOS or Linux (Windows-only; depends on Win32 APIs).
- Users wanting fully offline, no-key dictation as the default (this is cloud-first).
- Users wanting meeting transcription, speaker diarization, AI chat, notes, or team spaces.
- Users wanting dictation translation, audio-file import, or batch transcription.
- Users wanting zero-configuration with no API key.

## Key differentiators
1. **Narrow scope**: one job — hotkey to text at cursor — done fast and reliably.
2. **No focus stealing**: a WS_EX_NOACTIVATE layered pill; the target window keeps focus.
3. **Adaptive dual-mode hotkey**: hold-to-talk vs tap-for-hands-free, plus Esc cancel.
4. **Visible failure**: clipboard/paste failures are logged, surfaced in the UI, and the
   text is dumped to disk — no silent `return False`.
5. **Chinese-specific correction**: hallucination filtering, Traditional→Simplified,
   punctuation restoration, and a domain lexicon gathered from foreground window title
   and history (never the clipboard).
6. **Hot reload**: config changes apply in ~1 s without restarting the daemon.
7. **Small footprint**: lazy imports keep heavy deps (numpy/torch/funasr) off the idle path.

## Comparison to alternatives
- [OpenWhispr](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr): cross-platform all-in-one
  (dictation + meetings + AI agent + notes + team spaces, Electron). Vox is Windows-only
  and single-purpose, faster to start, smaller, focus-preserving.
- [local-speak](https://github.com/AKCodez/local-speak): fully local/offline, hold-key to
  type. Vox is cloud-first for speed with an opt-in local engine.
- [SenseType](https://github.com/Kuaias/SenseType): SenseVoice-based Chinese dictation.
  Vox adds a typed cloud fallback chain, visible-failure engineering, and a correction
  pipeline.
- [Wispr Flow](https://wisprflow.ai/): commercial, closed-source. Vox is MIT open source.
